description: When He's correcting us, it's because He loves us, not because He's done with us.
excerpt: That's the part we forget in a hard season. When life gets heavy and God feels quiet, the temptation is to assume He's walked away. He hasn't.
verse: "For no one is abandoned by the Lord forever."
body_html:
As a parent walking through hard seasons of discipline, I feel this one on both sides.

Discipline isn't fun. It costs me something to do it. Letting things slide would be easier. But if I actually love my kids, I don't get to look the other way. Love shows up even when it's hard, and a parent who never corrects isn't loving their kids. They're just absent.

God does the same thing with us.

The surrounding verses say He brings grief, but He also shows compassion because of His unfailing love. He doesn't enjoy causing sorrow. When He's correcting us, it's because He loves us, not because He's done with us.

That's the part we forget in a hard season. When life gets heavy and God feels quiet, the temptation is to assume He's walked away. He hasn't. His correction has a limit, and His compassion always comes back around.

Thank God He loves us enough to discipline us. And thank Him even more that He won't abandon us forever, no matter what season we're sitting in.

Where have you felt abandoned by God lately, and could what you're walking through actually be His love correcting you instead of His absence?
